Ok, before I give you psychology INTERNET advice, do note this is the internet. I have some skills, mostly people management, profiling (for business purposes) and negotiating, but what I say should be done with your research and analysis of what is going on.

Here is what I can see here. Something has happened to trigger her into a response like this. Some in people management call it a Dear John letter, as it has all the prose and wording similar to the Dear John letter in its traditional sense.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dear_John_letter

Traditionally it is used to close a point, but it can also be used to get a point across. If it used, it is usually an emotional response. Usually in frustration. Because there is no direct frustration in the message, it gives off the feeling of being in response to something else that does not involve you. EG, she is broke, had a bad relationship, is unhappy, depressed, misses something from home, but what I honestly think has happened is that she has attended some sort of self improvement seminar and she feels she needs to act on something and is not entirely sure how to do it. I am guessing something has been bugging her about you or something you did, or she did and this is her trying to resolve it.

The issue is, I do not feel it is genuine. As I said, she is trying to make amends, but something else has prompted it. It may not be her own volition. It may be a good thing (such as remorse, less likely), or a bad thing (such as trying to make amends in order to get a life line, most likely).
